correctness.rationale: With the stated counting-measure Fourier convention, cyclic averaging reduces the mass optimum to 1−3/min S. The phasor identity and integer gap smoothing identify the minimum: a gap at least n/2 gives S≥−1; otherwise smoothing gaps differing by at least two strictly lowers the cosine sum. The balanced triple has S<−1 for n≥5. For n=3 the equilateral triple attains the universal lower bound −3/2, and for n=4 the six distinct-root balanced characters and the three coincident/opposite-root characters give exactly nine minima at −1. The six balanced contacts have an invertible circulant matrix when 3∤n: the displayed factors vanish only at the excluded roots of unity, except the row sum 2σ_n, which is negative. Nonnegativity and symmetrization force all optimizers to satisfy those contacts. For 3|n the two contact equations are real-independent (one sum of real parts and one signed sum of imaginary parts); the autocorrelation is strict at every other character, proving dimension four. The Taylor coefficient checks. CHECKER.py was read, not executed; its LP and enumerations are finite corroboration, not the proof.
